facts.F261: The shipped build fails these: Home reports 424px and the main-wrapped pages 292px while the board reports 272px, so the all-pages equality fails and names each page; the Home start changes when the window widens, which the two window widths catch; a team name field reports about 1100px, which the cap reading catches; the default-team list, the expiry number field, the Matrix room field and the two dialog lists report the platform box, which the border, fill and face readings catch; the Teams Save sits in no section, the instance rename forms sit in indented bullet lists and the settings groups draw the raw UA fieldset border, which the section reading catches; Delete resolves the --cz-black fill, which the tier comparison against Save catches; and the two project headers show a text run with no element, while the two board links resolve an underline and no gap, which the attribute and gap readings catch. Each law also fails on its own plausible wrong implementation: deleting the main element rule instead of scoping it is caught by the /unsubscribe padding reading; padding the frame but leaving the centred Home column is caught by the window-width pair on Home alone; capping the frame width is caught by the board lane row, which must still use the window; applying the default cap globally instead of scoping it to the frame is caught twice, by the sign-in card field that would narrow and by the dialog title field that would stop short of its textarea; sizing a field with width instead of max-inline-size is caught by the 256-character unbroken value, which then pushes the document scrollWidth past its clientWidth; giving Delete a borderless quiet look is caught by the 3 to 1 boundary reading on it; moving the New issue trigger into the header row is caught by the search panel box after the slash key; renaming the report-link class or its /report href is caught by the live refresh, which then never arrives; leaving the change report header as the old text run is caught by its own data-key-prefix reading; changing the rename row outer element or its markers is caught by the two renames and their two refusals; naming a colour literal for the new surfaces is caught by check-arch S1; and editing the stylesheet without renaming it is caught by check-arch R2.
facts.F262: A FIELD IS AS WIDE AS WHAT IT HOLDS, FROM A CLOSED SET OF THREE SIZES, AND THE DEFAULT CAP IS SCOPED TO THE FRAMED FORMS. The shipped rule input[type=text], input[type=email], input[type=password], textarea { width: 100% } is what stretches a team name to about 1100px. Its width becomes inline-size, and a max-inline-size is taken from three size classes: .field--short (about 8rem, a token expiry or a count), .field--name (about 24rem, a team, project or workspace name), .field--long (about 36rem, an email, a URL or a Matrix room id). THE THREE CLASSES WORK WHEREVER THEY ARE NAMED; THE UNCLASSED DEFAULT CAP APPLIES ONLY INSIDE .app-shell__content. That scope is deliberate, because the shipped rule reaches text, email and password inputs in 22 templates, and two families of them are not framed forms. FIRST, the signed-out card pages delivered by ui-bare-pages (signin.html:9, forgot, bootstrap_claim, invite_accept, reset_password) sit in a 28rem .page-card with 1.75rem padding, which leaves about 24.5rem of content, so a 24rem default cap would visibly narrow every one of them; they are out of scope and must not change, so outside the frame a field keeps inline-size: 100% and no cap. SECOND, the dialogs: .modal-dialog is width: min(30rem, 92vw) with 1.5rem padding (foundry.8a68a324.css:864), so a capped title field would stop short while its description textarea ran the full dialog width. THE MODEL COVERS THE SUM ALGEBRA ONLY: it decides whether a declared chain of padding boxes yields one edge for every page at both viewports, and it refutes the three chains that do not. It does NOT read the stylesheet, resolve a selector, evaluate the cascade, or know whether the shipped file matches the chain it was given. THE ONLY CHECK OF THE REAL STYLESHEET IS THE BROWSER ALL-PAGES READING in the oracle: the computed inline start and block start of every framed page at both viewports, plus a reading of /unsubscribe, which is outside the frame and must keep its own page padding when the element rule is scoped. check-arch covers the asset and token-seam rules, never the geometry. TLA+ is not needed: there is no temporal, fairness or concurrency claim anywhere in this Request, every observation is of a settled document. Agda is not needed: no proof over an open domain is claimed. No model for the field sizes, the control family, the sections, the Delete tier or the board header: each names no shared state, no multi-step protocol and no crash window, and each domain is the closed set of named pages, named field kinds or named control kinds the finite laws enumerate. The one broad domain is the stored name or label a field must hold, carried by a generated property over the rendered page rather than by a model.
